Pool Deck Pavers · Windermere, FL

Travertine and Paver Pool Decks in Windermere

Pool deck pavers or travertine in Windermere run $12–$30 per sq ft installed as of October 2026. A lakefront deck overlay on the Butler Chain is built next to water Florida protects as an Outstanding Florida Water, which raises the stakes on keeping runoff and bedding sand out of the lake during the job, not just on the finished look.

By the Opera Concrete & Pavers estimating team · Updated October 1, 2026

Building next to an Outstanding Florida Water changes the job site, not the material

The Butler Chain of Lakes, the connected lake system Windermere sits among, on the isthmus between Lake Down and Lake Butler Wikipedia, Windermere, Florida, carries Florida's Outstanding Florida Water designation, a protection tier meant to stop new work from lowering a waterbody's existing quality FDEP, Outstanding Florida Waters fact sheet. A travertine or paver overlay on a deck close to that shoreline still uses the same base, bedding sand and edge restraint as any other job, but keeping bedding sand, demolition debris and wash water out of the lake during construction matters more here than on a yard a few streets back from the water.

The deck's own footprint still answers to the town's 0.45 cap

Windermere's impervious surface rule covers 'swimming pools' and the paved area around them inside its single 0.45 ceiling Windermere LDC, impervious surface, so overlaying an old concrete deck in travertine without changing its footprint doesn't add new impervious area, but widening it toward the lake does. A poured concrete deck on the same lot faces an identical footprint question, regardless of which surface finish gets picked.

Base Depth for a Paver Deck Follows the Patio Spec, Not the Driveway Spec

A paver pool deck carries the same light pedestrian load a patio does, lounge chairs, foot traffic, the occasional umbrella stand, so the ICPI minimum of 4 inches of compacted base on well-drained soil applies here too, not the heavier 6-inch driveway spec. What's different around a pool is how much more moisture the base near the water's edge sees from splash-out, backwash and equipment pad runoff, on top of whatever rain the rest of the yard gets. On a Windermere job, we treat the few feet closest to the coping as wetter ground by default and compact accordingly, even on a lot where the rest of the base tests dry.

Running the Pool Through a Paver Deck Install

A pool can usually stay open and chemically maintained through most of a paver deck job, since the work happens around the water rather than in it, as long as the equipment pad and its plumbing stay protected from excavation and compaction equipment nearby. We sequence the base and bedding work around any scheduled filter backwash or pool service visit rather than making the homeowner reschedule theirs. On a Windermere project, that coordination means the pool doesn't sit untreated and turning green while the paver field takes shape around it over several days of work.

A travertine overlay near the Butler Chain, worked out in square feet

Say a 680 square foot concrete pool deck near Lake Down is ready for a travertine overlay, with the yard sloping gently toward the shoreline about 40 feet from the pool cage. Pricing the overlay at $12–$30 per sq ft installed runs $8,160 to $20,400, tightening to roughly $9,520 to $14,960 in the typical $14–$22 range once the stone and pattern are picked. Because the lot sits inside the Butler Chain's protected boundary, the crew plans where wash water and old demolition material go before the first paver comes up, rather than routing it toward the lake by default.

Setting an Overlay System's Thickness at the Door Threshold

Pavers set over an existing concrete deck add real height, typically the bedding system plus the paver itself, and that buildup has to be checked against every door threshold, pool equipment housing and the coping line before the job starts, not after. We often shave a shallow setback into the old slab near a sliding door, or choose a thinner bedding system specifically at that transition, so the finished paver surface doesn't end up higher than the threshold it meets. On a Windermere overlay job, missing that check is how a finished deck ends up funneling rainwater back into the house at exactly the door people use most.

Slick Travertine and Algae Where the Deck Stays Wettest

Honed or polished travertine already has less texture than a textured concrete paver, and in the section of deck closest to the water, or any shaded stretch under a lanai roof, that smoother surface combined with algae film is where slip incidents on a pool deck tend to happen. A Windermere homeowner choosing a very smooth travertine finish for its look should weigh that against the splash zone's slip risk specifically, since a textured or tumbled finish holds up better underfoot in exactly the spot that stays wet longest. Regular cleaning reduces the algae side of that risk but doesn't change how slick polished stone gets when wet.

Re-Sanding Joints Near a Pool Needs a Shorter Interval

Joint sand anywhere in a paver field wears thin from rain and foot traffic over time, but the rows closest to a pool lose sand faster still, since splash-out and pool-service hose-downs wash sand out of those joints on top of normal weathering. Topping off and compacting joint sand in that zone on a shorter cycle than the rest of a Windermere deck, rather than waiting for the whole field to need it at once, keeps the pavers nearest the water from rocking before the rest of the deck shows any sign of wear at all.

Frequently asked questions

Does building near the Butler Chain of Lakes require a special state permit for a pool deck overlay?

Not simply for the overlay itself. The Outstanding Florida Water designation targets activities that would lower the chain's water quality, which matters most for work happening at or past the water's edge rather than a deck resurfacing set back from the shoreline.

Why does job-site runoff matter more on a Butler Chain lot?

Because the lakes carry Florida's highest water-quality protection tier. Keeping bedding sand, wash water and demolition debris from washing toward the shoreline during the job matters more here than it would on a yard well back from any lake.

Does overlaying an existing pool deck in travertine change its impervious footprint in Windermere?

Not if the deck's edges stay where they are. Widening the deck toward the lake while overlaying it does add new area against the town's 0.45 impervious cap, even though the overlay material itself doesn't.
